gloss: old rice; rice from a previous harvest

definitions.gloss: old rice; rice held over from a previous year's harvest
definitions.explanation: Rice harvested in an earlier year and stored, as opposed to {新米|しんまい}, the freshly harvested crop. It is still perfectly edible but drier and less fragrant, so it is priced lower and often blended with new rice.

examples.japanese: {古米|こまい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{安|やす}い→安い：00464_yasui⟧。
examples.english: Old rice is a little cheaper.

examples.japanese: {古米|こまい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{多|おお}め→多め：28421_oome⟧にして⟦{炊|た}く→炊く：02127_taku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧よい。
examples.english: It's best to cook old rice with a little extra water.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新米|しんまい}→新米：06877_shinmai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{古米|こまい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{混|ま}ぜて→混ぜる：02423_mazeru⟧⟦{売|う}っている→売る：00906_uru⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Some shops sell new and old rice blended together.

examples.japanese: {古米|こまい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦チャーハン→チャーハン：17671_chaahan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧パラパラ⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、かえっておいしく⟦{食|た}べられる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: Old rice comes out nice and loose when made into fried rice, so it actually tastes better that way.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古米|こまい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炊|た}く→炊く：02127_taku⟧: to cook old rice
- {古米|こまい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{新米|しんまい}→新米：06877_shinmai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{混|ま}ぜる→混ぜる：02423_mazeru⟧: to blend old and new rice
- {古古米|ここまい}: rice two harvests old (the next step down)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{新米|しんまい}→新米：06877_shinmai⟧: newly harvested rice — moist and aromatic, sold at a premium in autumn. Note that ⟦{新米|しんまい}→新米：06877_shinmai⟧ also means 'novice, rookie' when applied to a person; {古米|こまい} has no such figurative sense.

USAGE:
Japan's rice year runs from November, so rice from before that changeover becomes {古米|こまい}. The word appears mainly on price tags and in cooking advice rather than in everyday conversation.
